title: Progressive JSON envelopes, graceful truncation, and callable-tool telemetry (PRD)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: PRD: Define deterministic acceptance criteria and operational playbook for progressive/streamed structured JSON envelopes and function/tool call handoff semantics. Goal: enable customers to rely on partial, typed emissions for real-time UX while guaranteeing safe retry/fallback behavior for tool invocations and clear telemetry for debugging. Deliverables: schema contract, streaming truncation semantics, tool-call lifecycle events, observability hooks, and QA test matrix.
scope: In scope: envelope wire-format for streamed partial objects, explicit truncation and resume behavior, function-call idempotency signals, telemetry hooks (emit/ack/error), backpressure guidance for SDKs, and e2e acceptance tests. Out of scope: model-level decoder changes, SDK language-specific client implementations (only spec + minimal JS reference), and billing changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Envelope contract: a top-level streamed protocol is documented such that every emission is a self-describing frame string (type, seq_id, durable_id_opt, payload_serialization) and the spec includes canonical examples for success, partial, error, and truncated frames.

2) Partial-object safety: consumers can reconstruct a deterministic JSON object stream by concatenating ordered 'object_fragment' frames and applying a final 'commit' frame; missing fragments produce a recoverable 'partial_committed' state rather than silent corruption.

3) Graceful truncation: when the runtime truncates output for token/latency/cost reasons, it must emit a final 'truncated' frame with fields: reason, truncated_at_seq, available_resume_token. SDKs and server-side reconstructor can map truncated->resume flow; acceptance tests verify roundtrip resume semantics with synthetic sequences.

4) Tool-call lifecycle: function/tool invocations are represented as 'tool_request' frames (tool_id, call_id, schema_hint, args_hash) followed by one or more 'tool_progress' frames and a terminal 'tool_result' or 'tool_error' frame. If the model emits a tool_request and the platform fails to deliver the call (timeout/queue-drop), platform must emit 'tool_declined' with failure_reason and fallback_model_id.

5) Idempotency and replay: each tool_request includes a durable_id or client-provided idempotency_key; acceptance tests assert that retries with the same durable_id produce at-most-once visible side-effects for registered test tools in the sandbox harness.

6) Error taxonomy: runtime must classify failures into 'transient', 'permanent', 'partial-result', and 'schema-violation' with clear operator playbook mapping (retry/backoff/fallback); CLI/console must surface specific failure codes in traces and logs.

7) Observability hooks: every frame must attach a stable trace_id and optional token_cost estimate; traces enable correlating emitted frames to token-level cost in the Console within 5 seconds of completion for hosted requests (tested with synthetic load).

8) Backpressure and SLOs: when throughput exceeds batching latency SLOs, the runtime may switch to 'headroom' mode and emit 'backpressure_advisory' frames; acceptance asserts advisory emission within 200ms of threshold breach and SDK gracefully surfaces advisory to caller.

9) Streaming consistency: e2e tests validate that consuming clients reconstruct the same logical object when fed frames from: (a) an uninterrupted stream, (b) a stream with a simulated transient disconnect followed by resume using resume_token, and (c) a truncated initial stream followed by a resumed call from available_resume_token.

10) Telemetry & debugging: Console UI and logs must show an ordered timeline of frames for any request (frame types, seq ids, tool ids, durations) and link to associated GitHub PR or Confluence note when a failure is triaged; acceptance includes sample console screenshot and a linked dashboard panel for the feature.

11) Backward compatibility: when a legacy client (no resume_token support) encounters 'truncated' frames, the platform must provide a best-effort 'finalized_object' fallback frame to preserve basic UX rather than returning raw fragments.

12) Security gating: tool_request frames that reference sensitive integrations must be gated by RBAC flags; automated tests assert that requests lacking required RBAC are returned as 'tool_declined' with audit log entries.

13) Performance: under test harness (p50 token latency target 75ms), progressive envelope overhead must add <10% CPU on the serving pod compared to baseline unframed streaming; load test artifacts included in QA.
14) Documentation & sample harness: PRD includes a complete conformance test suite and a minimal JS/HTTP harness that demonstrates resume, retry, and tool-call flows.
15) Sign-off: PM, Runtime ENG lead, Console ENG lead, and Security must sign acceptance; sign-off recorded as appended comment in the ticket and the final Confluence page.
qa_test_cases: TC-1: Reconstruct full object from uninterrupted frame stream (happy path).
TC-2: Resume after simulated TCP drop using resume_token; reconstructed object matches TC-1.
TC-3: Receive truncated frame and verify 'finalized_object' fallback for legacy client mode.
TC-4: Emit tool_request then simulate platform delivery failure; assert 'tool_declined' emitted and audit log entry present.
TC-5: Idempotency test: replay same durable_id twice; side-effect count == 1 for sandbox tool.
TC-6: Schema violation frame emitted and consumer receives 'schema-violation' code; Console shows linked trace.
TC-7: Backpressure advisory emitted under synthetic overload; SDK surfaces advisory callback.
TC-8: Security gating: unauthorized tool_request returns 'tool_declined' and audit shows user+caller context.
TC-9: Performance regression test comparing baseline with envelope enabled under p50/p95 load.
TC-10: Telemetry correlation: frame timeline in Console links to token cost panel for the request.
notes: Decisions and trade-offs: We chose a typed-frame streaming approach (frames-as-lines) to avoid ambiguous partial JSON parsing in clients; trade-off is slightly larger wire overhead but stronger determinism for resume and tooling. We decided the platform will own resume_tokens (opaque strings) rather than model-emitted tokens to simplify replay logic. Operator playbook artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Progressive+JSON+Envelopes, reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2241, test harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-example.
